line.comment: * SCRIPT NAME: ZH.Build.OWP
* DESCRIPTION: Builds one Medium OWP for a $race.
* NPC OWPs are placed 5-10km away from the Outpost, toward the sector center.
* $race: the faction building the OWPs.
* $isFree: if [TRUE], bypasses construction costs during galaxy initialization.
* $posArray: specified XYZ and sector; null for automatic NPC placement.
* Returns the constructed OWP, or null.
* AUTHOR: DATE: 10 October 2026
* OWP construction uses the same quality for costing and creation.
* Players must specify a position and always pay.
* Faction-wide OWP cap.
* Player: sector and position are already provided. Cost is adjusted by supply.
* Obtain the construction Outpost directly.
* NPC: Rank and attempt eligible Outposts.
* Randomize before ranking for randomized tie-breaking.
* Important: Explicit forward traversal. The ranked array is sorted highest score first.
* Determine NPC construction position.
* Build in this sector if possible.
* Shared construction logic.
* Verify Outpost and sector ownership.
* Only one Medium OWP per sector, as NPC.
* No construction while hostile capital ships are present.
* Check the normal ship construction costs.
* Mayhem.BuildShip initializes the platform. Position array contains X, Y, Z, and sector.
* Charge construction materials and player population.
* Find an NPC construction position.
* Distance from Outpost to sector center.
* Choose 5-10km from the Outpost.
* Move toward the sector center.
* Outpost is at the sector center.
* Avoid collisions with existing objects.
* GetValidPos already returns XYZ and sector.
* Check that collision adjustment preserved our distance restriction.
* Invalid position. Try again.
* Rank NPC Outposts by strategic importance.
* Highest scores are evaluated first.
* Skip sectors already defended by an OWP.
* Base economic and strategic sector value.
* De jure sector.
* Border sector.
* Geographic bottleneck.
* Hostile neighboring faction.
* Sort Outposts by their strategic scores.
* MSCI sorts ascending, so reverse for highest-first.
